Bewilder

bih-WIL-der · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To bewilder is to cause someone to become completely confused.

The airport's last-minute gate changes bewildered even seasoned travelers who thought they knew the terminal well.

Worked Example

The substitute teacher's contradictory instructions bewildered the class, and half the students ended up doing the wrong assignment entirely.

Bewilder describes overwhelming, disorienting confusion -- not mild puzzlement, but a real loss of bearings.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

flummox: to confuse or puzzle someone thoroughly

disorient: to make someone lose their sense of direction or understanding

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

orient: to help someone understand a new situation clearly

guide: to show someone the way clearly and confidently

Where it sits · how completely the confusion takes over — puzzle → bewilder → dumbfound

puzzle vs. bewilder: Puzzle is milder than bewilder: a tricky crossword clue may puzzle you for a minute before it clicks, but to be bewildered is to be completely lost in confusion.

dumbfound vs. bewilder: To be dumbfounded is to be left utterly speechless with shock, beyond simple confusion.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — be-

prefix — be-: thoroughly, completely (Old English be-)

root — wilder

root — wilder: to lead into the wild; lose one's way (Old English/Germanic wild)

Put it together

Put it together: Bewilder combines be- ("thoroughly") with wilder ("lead into the wild, lose one's way") -- literally to lead someone thoroughly into the wilderness, which came to mean leaving them completely confused and lost.

Use the root in a new word: wilderness
